newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil reserves to hit $70 bln in '97 - paper.
newsitem.headline: Brazil reserves to hit $70 bln in '97 - paper.

text.p: Brazil's foreign reserves will grow to about $70 billion in 1997, up from $60 billion at the end of 1996, Central Bank International Affairs Director Gustavo Franco told O Globo newspaper.
"I think what is most likely is that there will be an increase in reserves similar to what we saw in 1996 (when they grew by $10 billion)," Franco told O Globo in an interview.

Franco said the trend toward attracting more investment through the stock market and foreign direct investment, versus short-term speculation in the money market, would continue this year. "The hot money is leaving because domestic interest rates are very similar to the rates charged globally for Brazil risk," he said.

Franco, who is closely identified with Brazil's foreign exchange rate policy, said Brazil's strong reais currency was not the reason for the country's increasingly poor export performance. He said only time and a committment to open market policies would get Brazilian exports industries in shape to compete on a global level.

"Poor export performance has a long history in this country...For thirty years, our economic model did not promote exports but import substitution, self-reliance, lower competitivity and declining productivity," Franco said.
